the argument system rejectAll, whose verifier rejects every proof, satisfies Sound with ε = 0

theorem rejectAll_sound : Sound rejectAll (fun _ => 0)
What the statements do not say
  • That a statement says what is meant. Lean checks that each theorem follows from the definitions that it names and, for each, the build reports no axiom beyond Lean's three standard ones; Lean does not check that these are the right definitions. That is read off the statements and the definitions under them. This page prints them for that, as far as it goes: three values are black boxes here (What this page does not show, below). The statements: sound, soundAndBinding, completeOnCanServe, zeroKnowledgeOnCanServe, refusedHandsOutNoProof, repliesFit, with the definition leanVerifier. These seven are this library's own wording of what is to be proved. So are the statements of soundness, completeness and zero knowledge as an IOP, which this page does not print (their files: lean/LIMITS.md, under "That a statement says what is meant").
  • That Lean's kernel, which checks the proofs, is free of bugs: it is trusted, not proved correct, as are the compilers, the operating system and the fetched packages. The pinned version of Lean, 4.29.1, predates the published fixes (from version 4.32.1 on) for soundness bugs in Lean's kernel and runtime and in the arbitrary-precision arithmetic library (GMP) that its Linux builds link against. No proof in this library is known to use such a bug; the proofs have not been searched for one, and the check script's word list and audit would not detect one. These pages do not report any check of the library with a later version of Lean. (lean/LIMITS.md, L45.) Lean's kernel has checked each of the six theorems with a larger thread stack than the default: the library that contains them is compiled with that setting, because with the default stack the kernel fails on some constants used by its theorems (lean/LIMITS.md, L69).
  • Fiat–Shamir. That a concrete hash function behaves as a uniformly random function (§5).
  • Second hash function. Technically, the IOP itself uses a second, fixed hash function, built from BLAKE2b's compression function. By the rules of the file format (docs/format/FORMAT.md, R15.3) it is used to digest public data (the scale file, lines of the parameter file, and the model's lookup tables, which the parameter file names by these digests) and the request. The theorems assume no property of it. The Fiat–Shamir heuristic then also assumes that blake2bHash behaves like a random function that is independent of it (The second hash function). None of these uses is essential to the protocol: the digest of the request is redundant, and the digests of public data can be made with the main hash function. The second hash function will be removed in a future version.
  • Exact match. That the public files specify the exact-match policy (the field exactMatch of FilesTaken, §4.4): the verifier does not check this, and the theorem sound applies only to such files (A public setup). The serving scripts use a different, tolerant policy, and the six theorems do not apply to it.
  • Intended files. That a commitment belongs to a single set of public files: no theorem ties a commitment to one set of public files or one policy. The user must therefore keep the intended public files together with the commitment.
  • Scales. That the model does anything at the settings that the public files specify: for some valid choices of the quantization scales, the outputs of the value and up projections are all zero, so no layer changes the residual stream (checked by hand, not proved; see the card PublicSetup). No theorem or test on this page determines which scale files have such scales.
  • Files fixed first. Anything about a provider that chooses its public files, or tries many, with access to the hash function: in the statements the files are fixed before the hash function is sampled. There is room to try many: the committer chooses the scale file, and five numbers of the parameter file are free, within what the parser of the files accepts (Judging the assumptions on the public files and on hash values).
  • Hash values treated alike. That the protocol treats all values of the hash function alike. Consider a protocol whose verifier accepts every request whenever one particular answer of the hash function has one particular value. A function sampled at random gives that value with probability 2^-256, so the protocol can still satisfy the statements. The value can be chosen to be the one that the concrete hash function gives; the verifier then accepts every request when instantiated with the concrete hash function (Judging the assumptions on the public files and on hash values).
  • Anything about running time. The bounds count queries to the hash function.
  • Anything about an adversary that queries the hash function in superposition: in the statements the committer, the prover and the malicious verifier query it classically, one bit string at a time (RandomizedAlgorithm, §8; MaliciousVerifier, §6.2).
  • That a program that runs on a machine computes ArgumentSystem.accepts, or that a prover program computes prove. These are facts about programs. The honest prover in these statements is a definition, not a program.
  • How the integer model relates to a model in floating-point arithmetic.
  • That the empty output is rejected: it has no position to check, so it is the model's output in the sense of §1 for every prompt and all weights, and when the extractor outputs weights, Sound does not count its acceptance as a failure.
  • A soundness bound for several proofs under one commitment: Sound concerns one proof. For N proofs submitted together, a union bound gives N times the error of one proof, evaluated at the number of hash queries of the whole list. For proofs checked one after another, no bound is stated.
  • Anything about several requests in one proof. The statement on zero knowledge concerns many replies under one commitment (§6.3).
  • Anything about a party that learns the committer's randomness or the weights by means other than the replies.
  • A bound on what the bits of many requests together reveal about the weights (§6.1, requestOutcome).
  • A security level: finalSoundnessError q, about q / 2^124 + 2^-101, is a bound on the soundness error, not a security level (see the card sound).
  • That the limit on the number of replies is respected: the prover does not count replies, so nothing in it enforces the number 688,127 in the theorems on zero knowledge (§6.4).
  • What the three public files reveal about the weights: the scale file of a fitted model is computed from its weights, and the theorems on zero knowledge do not cover this (§6.3).
  • That any public files other than one stored set form a public setup: the library proves this for one set (filesInUse_stored), whose scale file is that of an example with synthetic weights (according to the header of Ladder/Stored.lean, not a theorem).
  • That a proof cannot be altered: the joint verification reads only those digests in the Merkle paths that it needs, so a typed proof can be altered at the others and still be accepted; and it is not proved anywhere that an accepted proof string cannot be changed elsewhere into another accepted one. This is malleability of the proof string, not a gap in soundness (§4.2).
What this page does not show
  • What this page contains. Every statement, and every definition that the introduction asks a reader who checks only soundness to read. It does not show the definitions of three Lean terms, which it treats as black boxes: FlashProve's description, the test on the public files (protocolDataWellFormed) and the honest provers and settings (honestProversAndSettings). Their sizes are under “Counts of declarations” above.
  • The line noncomputable section. Many definitions on the cards are inside such a section, which no card shows, so a def on a card may be one that Lean does not compile. leanVerifier, flashProve, compile, compiledVerifier and finalVerifierProgram are inside one; verdictOf, whose three parts the command lean-verify evaluates, is not.
  • What the proof of sound depends on. Among other things, it uses theorems of coding theory from files that are adapted from others' work (lean/CREDITS.md). Nothing in these coding-theory files has a card here. The axioms that Lean lists for sound cover them, as they cover every file on which the proof depends.
  • Properties that the library states but does not prove for any object: G3'pol, G7', G7'bits and the six Package… statements (Ladder.lean, Ladder/Bits.lean, Ladder/Package.lean). None of them is used in the statements of the six theorems or in the definitions under these. The plain properties Complete and ZeroKnowledge are discussed in §6: ZeroKnowledge is not proved for any system, and Complete is proved only for a verifier that accepts everything (acceptAll_complete).

Judging the assumptions on the public files and on hash values

The assumptions Files fixed first and Hash values treated alike (above) can be judged only from the protocol's definitions. A reader can check the following.

  • Files fixed first. Is the digest of the public files, or their bytes, part of the query whose answer is the commitment and of every query from which the verifier samples a challenge (directly or through the instance)? Is any answer of the hash function compared with bytes of the public files?
  • Hash values treated alike. Do the definitions single out any value of the hash function, whether written out, referred to by name, or computed?

We have read FlashProve's own definitions with both questions in mind. The findings below come from reading the definitions, not from theorems.

  • Files fixed first. Their digest is the first input of every sequence of chained queries, and it is included in the encoding of the key, whose hash is the commitment. It is not part of the instance, which consists of the request only (a window of tokens, one further token and two positions; the online IOP adds the out-of-domain seed and answer of the copy, §6.4). For comparisons, see the next item.
  • Hash values treated alike. By reading and by counting occurrences, we found no place where an answer of the sampled hash function is compared with a stored digest or with bytes of the public files (lean/GAPS.md, 51). The compiler's verifier does compare such answers with the commitment and with digests in the proof (for example verifyDigestKey). The definitions used by verify do contain one explicit answer of the concrete hash function, namely a digest of the stored public files; as far as we can tell from reading, it is not used anywhere.

No attack is known, and neither point is settled by a theorem (lean/GAPS.md, 5 and 51).

Appendix A. FlashProve's protocol

This page prints 1,558 declarations. The statement of the theorem sound depends on about 17,000 named declarations of the library (counted as described in §11); the page prints those nearest to it, and the protocol's three IOPs, the compiler, BLAKE2b and the integer model. The rest are in the files, most of them under Johnson/Desc/, OnBytes/Model/, OnBytes/Params/, OnBytes/Iop/ and Inst/Model/.

A protocol is a linkable holographic IOP, from which the verifier is built. It makes no queries to the random oracle. It has an encoder that encodes an index, here the weights, as an oracle string, with a decoder; an out-of-domain sample on each encoding; and three interactive oracle proofs: offline, link and online.

An IOP is defined for a batch of instances: one prover serves them together, and each instance has its own verifier.

This appendix gives the three IOPs from which FlashProve.flashProveDescription is assembled. The first folded sections contain the Lean definitions nearest to the six theorems: the verifier's side, the public files, the honest provers and settings. Next are the terms of this appendix, a count of sub-protocols by kind, and each IOP, sub-protocol by sub-protocol. The last folded sections contain the protocol itself: the format in which an IOP is written, how a written IOP is run, the public checks on it, the two decisions, the three IOPs chain by chain, the kinds of sub-protocol, and the assembly.

This appendix shows the verifier's side of the protocol and, in the folds named here, the honest provers. The honest provers and settings of the six theorems are on the card honestProversAndSettings, in What the theorems refer to.

  • Three folded sections, from The honest provers and settings: one closed term to The three honest provers of the interactive protocol, expand it down to honestProvers.
  • Six later folds, from The three provers to The components of a prover, expand the offline and the online prover down to one round's message, and the link's prover down to linkSide. The last of them contains the types of which these two provers are made, and can be read first.

The fixed-message provers, the constant committer and the constant prover in this appendix supply fields of the protocol's record, which the types need and which neither compile nor the verifier reads. Fixed-message provers are provers that send the same messages whatever the weights, and so show nothing of them; at public files in use (FilesInUse, §4.4) the protocol's honest provers are different provers: only where a function that makes them refuses do they fall back on these. The constant committer is a committer that returns one constant whatever the weights, and so commits to nothing; the committer of the six theorems is a different committer: the one that compile makes (Johnson/Face/Compiler.lean), which encodes the weights and hashes the key. The constant prover returns empty strings.

def InScope (Z : PublicFiles) : Bool :=
Layout file

the layout file is that of the stored full-size example (Ladder/Stored.lean)

Reader

the reader (readFiles) accepts the three files

Parameter file

the parameter file equals that example's byte for byte, except for the eight free numbers (FreeLines), which are written as the reader read them; and 2^8 ≤ theta. Hence only the scale file and these eight numbers are free, within what the reader accepts. All security settings, the version line and the layout are fixed, so files of a changed format are out of scope.

decide (Z.pol = policyFile (freeLinesOf pp)) && decide (2 ^ 8 ≤ pp.pol.theta)
| .error _ => false
Remark

Policies that leave every counted token unconstrained remain in scope: (256, 256, 1) for requests with one counted token, and theta = C with cap = 1,024 for every request.

Why 2^8 ≤ theta: every token costs at least 2^8. For smaller theta, no output with a counted token meets the policy (theta < C), or the policy bounds little except the number of counted tokens (theta = C). ("Cost" and "counted token": see MeetsPolicy.)

One round: a prover message, consisting of an oracle part and a plain part that is read in full, followed by a challenge. The compiler (Compile/) takes only oracles that are strings. Linear oracles also fit the type, but no other file of this library mentions them.

structure Round where
Oracle part

the oracle part, an abstract type. For oracles that are strings, Orc = ∀ p, Sym p; for linear oracles, a vector. A message without oracles has Orc = Unit

Orc : Type

the queries p. For linear oracles, linear functionals. A message without oracles has Pos = Empty

Pos : Type

the answers to a query p

Sym : Pos → Type

how Orc is read by queries. For oracles that are strings, this is function application (see Round.IsPoint)

rd : Orc → (p : Pos) → Sym p
Plain part

the plain part. A message without a plain part has Plain = Unit

Plain : Type
Challenge

the challenge, uniform in the finite set Chal. A round without a challenge has Chal = Unit

Chal : Type
Fixed message

a fixed message of the right format: its oracle part and its plain part

/-- a fixed message of the right format: what is sent where there is no honest message, and after
a rejection of an earlier part, when the later rounds still take place (by convention) -/
dOrc : Orc
dPlain : Plain

the list of all challenges; Chal is not empty

/-- the list of all challenges, behind a function of `Unit`: compiled Lean is strict, and builds
the list only where this function is called -/
finChalT : Unit → Fintype Chal := by lazy_instance
[neChal : Nonempty Chal]

The numbers:

  • at most 44,040,191 columns of one table may be read in total
  • the offline IOP's verifier reads at most 62 columns, the link IOP's verifier at most 62 on the first table and at most 62 on the copy, and the online IOP's verifier at most 64 per request (proved for public files in scope: readsG_atFiles, one_atFiles)
  • no out-of-domain seed is excluded (the last field, the probability that a seed is outside the set that the theorem allows, is 0)
  • The arguments are the number of runs of the online IOP on one copy, the errors of the three simulators and three measures of the parts of the abort sets that may depend on the private input

⟨44040191, 62, 62, 62, 64, s1, zT, zL, zO, hT, hL, hO, 0⟩

In words
In Lean · Ladder.lean, lines 247–247

The maximum number of hash queries that one run each of the honest sampler, committer and prover may make together. The value is a design choice.

  • RepliesFit imposes this bound, via WithinBudget, on the total for one run each of the sampler, the committer and the prover (one commitment and one request, not a batch)
  • in bindingErrorInQueries it accounts for one run of the committer
  • Statements of Ladder.lean that are not among the six theorems require it of commit and of D's own parser, for files in scope
  • Each query counts as one, regardless of its length; a typed query of the compiler counts as one query for each digest of its answer
def honestBudget : ℕ := 2 ^ 48

K3.proverSideOfLookupInChain (K3.keyOwners K.look1.face) K.reads K.jobs1 K.wit K.look1, K.rng,

Shared chain

sharedChainProverSidesInOrder (K14.proverSidesOfSharedRounds K.lin K.weights) (K14.proverSidesOfSharedSendings K.send K.weights fun c => randK14 (K.rand c))
++ [K.onU, K.onOmega]
Second chain

second := [K.own]

what the second chain's sides are given at their start

meet := K.meet
Remark

In these folded sections the chains are named after their Lean fields first, shared and second. These are chains 1, 2 and 3 of the table of terms, so "the second chain" here is the table's third chain.

In a Lean name, K followed by a number denotes a kind of sub-protocol; the fifteen kinds are listed below in this appendix. The kinds here are oracle message with out-of-domain sample (K1; a "sending" in Lean names), product-tree lookup argument (K3), proximity test with linear constraints (K12), committed-table claim merge (K13; "the batching" in these folded sections) and committed-table claim reduction (K14; the shared chain's own rounds in these folded sections). The two sub-protocols of K14.proverSidesOfSharedSendings are of kind K1.

The offline prover's arguments: 25 fields, among them the stored table's columns, the readers, the oracle messages, the lookups, the proximity tests, the batching and the shared chain's data.

structure KeyParts (W₀ Rc X₀ X Wk : Type) where
/-- the stored table's columns -/
stored : W₀ → Rc → Nat → Nat → Option (List Cb.Gl.F)
inRange : W₀ → Bool
dummy : W₀
own₀ : X
ownShared₀ : X₀
meet : X → State (In2 W₀ Rc) X₀ → X
/-- the index's reader -/
weights : W₀ → Weights
/-- the reader of the committer's coins -/
rand : Rc → TableRand
/-- the three sendings of the first chain -/
idx : K1.SendJob (In1 W₀ Rc) X
msg : K1.SendJob (In1 W₀ Rc) X
w : K1.SendJob (In1 W₀ Rc) X
/-- the two lookups: one reader of points; each lookup has a job of its own, because the two have
different faces and a job sees no face -/
reads : K3.Reads
jobs0 : K3.LookJobs Wk
jobs1 : K3.LookJobs Wk
wit : In1 W₀ Rc → Wk
look0 : K3.At
look1 : K3.At
/-- the proximity test on the ranges' group: A LETTER -/
rng : Placed (In1 W₀ Rc) (In1 W₀ Rc) X
/-- the batching -/
pile : K13.PileOf KeyInst
batt : VerifiableInference.Desc.K13.Where
/-- the shared chain's own rounds and its two sendings -/
lin : K14.Data
send : K14.SendPub
/-- the two proximity tests of the shared chain: LETTERS -/
onU : Placed Empty (In2 W₀ Rc) X₀
onOmega : Placed Empty (In2 W₀ Rc) X₀
/-- the proximity test of the second chain: A LETTER -/
own : Placed (In1 W₀ Rc) (In1 W₀ Rc) X

def sharedChainProverSidesInOrder (own send : List (Placed Empty (In2 W₀ Rc) X₀)) : List (Placed Empty (In2 W₀ Rc) X₀) :=

The numbers of a proximity test at a place, as the verifier's description reads them (P12: a proximity test's parameters). If the place's chain differs from the chain of the numbers, or the numbers yield no rounds, the value is noP12 at that place, in which all other numbers are 0, all lists are empty and both flags are false.

def proximityTestParametersAt (place : Place) (x : PlaceNums) : P12 :=
if place.chain != x.chain then noP12 place else
match testOracles5 x.nums x.firstGroup with
| some os =>
{ place := place, nums := x.nums, idx := x.idx, oracles := os,
before := beforeOf x.chain x.nums, answers := x.answers, early := x.early }
| none => noP12 place

def honestProversByCopyNumber : Family (batchOf C D tF tJ t3 F silent).loc (W₀ × Rc × Sd) where
Coin := (honestBatchProverOfFile C D tF tJ t3 F silent B H (J 0) sh ext).one.Coin
finCoin := (honestBatchProverOfFile C D tF tJ t3 F silent B H (J 0) sh ext).one.finCoin
neCoin := (honestBatchProverOfFile C D tF tJ t3 F silent B H (J 0) sh ext).one.neCoin
ext := fun _ => ext
strat := fun n => (honestBatchProverOfFile C D tF tJ t3 F silent B H (J n) sh ext).one.strat
Bad := (honestBatchProverOfFile C D tF tJ t3 F silent B H (J 0) sh ext).one.Bad
Hid := fun n => (honestBatchProverOfFile C D tF tJ t3 F silent B H (J n) sh ext).one.Hid

After a round's challenge, the round is added to the ChainProgress. If computing the message or adding the round returns an error, the ChainProgress halts but the round is still added. If there is no Step, it halts and no round is added.

def progressAfterChallenge (L : Lay) (z : ChainProgress S Cl W Y) (s : Option (Step W Y)) (d : Fmt.Drawn) : ChainProgress S Cl W Y :=
match s with
| none => z.halt
| some s =>
match z.say s with
| .error _ =>
((z.halt.heard L s (subTold s.decl s.oracles) d).toOption).getD
(z.push s (subTold s.decl s.oracles) d)
| .ok x =>
match z.heard L s x d with
| .ok z' => z'
| .error _ => ((z.halt.heard L s x d).toOption).getD (z.push s x d)

variable {S Cl Xi V W X W₀ Rc Ky Tr X₀ G P C C' V' W' Y : Type}

A prover, given as lists of sides. In these folded sections the chains are named after their Lean fields: first, shared and second are chains 1, 2 and 3 of the table of terms, so "the second chain" here is the table's third chain.

structure Prover (W₀ Rc Xi Ky Tr X₀ X : Type) where
Input

the stored tables' columns stored

/-- the stored tables' columns, by the statement's item and the position, typed in the field, as a
table's symbol is; `Prover.storedWords` converts them to words; `none`: no column there:
`fillCols` then takes the stored run's column or returns an error -/
stored : W₀ → Rc → Nat → Nat → Option (List Cb.Gl.F)

a request's trace trace

/-- a request's trace: a function, which `ready` applies; `none` if there is none -/
trace : W₀ → Xi → Option Tr

a function key of the public instance; its value is what the shared chain's sides are given of the instance

/-- the key: what the prover's sides in the shared chain are given of the public instance: a
function, which `ready` applies. It is meant for the stored table's out-of-domain seeds and
answers. It is no part of Rc and no coin of a run. No type compares it with what `FileDescription.start₂`
reads -/
key : Xi → Ky

the range test inRange, and a named element dummy

/-- in range: a test on what all requests share. `run` applies it to w₀ -/
inRange : W₀ → Bool
/-- a named element of W₀: `readyTests` returns an error unless `inRange` is true of it, so a
prover that passes has a range that is not empty. No other function of this file reads it -/
dummy : W₀

what the parts pass on at the start of the first chain and of the shared chain: own₀, ownShared₀

/-- what the parts pass on, at the start of the first chain -/
own₀ : X
/-- the same at the start of the shared chain -/
ownShared₀ : X₀
Chains

the sides of the first, shared and second chains: first, shared, second

first : List (Placed (Local W₀ Rc Xi Tr) (Local W₀ Rc Xi Tr) X)
shared : List (Placed Empty (Common W₀ Rc Ky) X₀)
second : List (Placed (Local W₀ Rc Xi Tr) (Local W₀ Rc Xi Tr) X)

what the second chain's sides are given at their start: meet

/-- what the second chain's prover's sides are given at their start, from what the first chain's
passed on and from the shared chain's end, as `FileDescription.start₃` does for the verifier -/
meet : X → State (Common W₀ Rc Ky) X₀ → X

variable {S Cl Xi V W X W₀ Rc Ky Tr X₀ G P C C' V' W' Y : Type}

The prover's side of consecutive rounds.

structure Part (V W X : Type) where

the coins that it takes: takes, spends, carries

/-- its own coins -/
takes : Due
/-- the entries of the book with `once := true` that name it, in the book's order: their names and
their counts. `lend` compares both with the book -/
spends : List (String × Due)
/-- the entries with `once := false` that name it, in the book's order: their names and counts -/
carries : List (String × Due)

its two abort conditions bad and hid, which the Lean comments call stops

/-- the first stop, asked before each of the part's rounds and once more after its last: from the
challenges before the part (in the second chain: the first and the second chain's alone, without
the shared chain's: `Ready.start₃`), and the part's own so far. No coin and no input, by type. In
the first and the second chain it takes the place of the library's `Bad`, in the shared chain of
its `stop0` (`Iop.BatchHonestProver`, Iop/Batch.lean). No default -/
bad : List Fmt.Drawn → List Fmt.Drawn → Option String
/-- the second stop, asked as the first is, and given V too: in the first and the second chain V
is the prover's whole input, the index and the stored tables' pads and encoding randomness
included (`Face.own`). It takes the place of the library's `Hid`, which is the library's name for
a set of challenges and says nothing on a property. No coin of the run, by type. In the shared
chain V is `Empty`: there the library has no such field. No default -/
hid : V → List Fmt.Drawn → List Fmt.Drawn → Option String

for each abort condition, a stated number, which is not a bound: badShare, hidShare

/-- a stated number, no bound: the number stated for the share of the lists of
challenges at which the first stop stops the part. Nothing compares it with the stop: that the
share is at most this has to be proved by whoever relies on it. The library measures such sets as
probabilities over uniform challenges (`prB`, Hiop/RecInterface.lean). A part whose stop never
fires states 0 of 1. No default -/
badShare : Odds
/-- the same for the second stop, at every V. No default -/
hidShare : Odds

one move for each round: moves

moves : List (Move (Handed takes spends carries) W X)

def proverSidesOfSharedRounds (P : Data) (weights : W₀ → Weights) : List (Placed Empty (Common W₀ Rc Ky) X) :=

p.lift (fun v => v) (fun c => ⟨entriesOf P.S (weights c.w₀)⟩) (fun _ => ()) fun x _ => x

if P.S.sharedSplitNeeded then [⟨place 8, [lifted (splitPart P)]⟩] else []

variable (files : PublicFiles) (parts : Parts files)
open Classical in

The format's salt prefixes for honestProvers. If honestProvers equals honestProversGivenDescriptions at some arguments, they are formatSaltStartsGivenDescriptions at these arguments, transported along that equality by saltStartsAlongEquation; otherwise they are zeroSaltStarts.

def saltStartsAtHonestProvers : SaltStarts (HonestProvers.ofThreeProvers (honestProvers files parts)) :=
if h : ∃ (description : OfflineDescription) (returned : OnlineReturn files) (places : H2U.Places4)
(firstChain : Chain TS ProofFile.Cl),
honestProvers files parts = honestProversGivenDescriptions files parts description returned places firstChain then
saltStartsAlongEquation files h.choose_spec.choose_spec.choose_spec.choose_spec (formatSaltStartsGivenDescriptions files parts _ _ _ _)
else zeroSaltStarts _

A scheme of type ZKCP.Arg. Its committer and prover are built from those of readOneF: they query the first hash block of each answer, and the other blocks if the test more returns true on that first block. The committer then queries the hash function for the digest of the key's code (ZKCP.keyDigest). κ maps the key and ϖ the proof. Its verifier is Vf.

def committerAndProverOverOneHash : ZKCP.Arg 256 J (List Token × List Token) Unit K'
(FullKey 256 R.protocol R.offlineRoundSplits R.linkRoundSplits × (T.D × Isk 256 R.protocol R.LeafBody R.offlineRoundSplits R.linkRoundSplits)) P' where
C := fun w => ((readOneF T h more).C (idx w)).bind fun keys =>
(ZKCP.keyDigest (fun ck : KeyT R => T.encT (ck.1, lowKey ck.2)) keys.1).mapO fun dg =>
(κ dg keys.1.2, (keys.1.2, keys.2))
P := fun isk x' _ => ((readOneF T h more).P isk.2 (instOf R x₀ x') ()).mapO (ϖ isk.1)
V := Vf
The terms of this appendix

The protocol's objects.

termwhat it means in this appendixthe Lean's word
public filesThree byte strings, parameters of the whole argument system: the parameter file, the layout file and the scale file.VerifierAndGoals.PublicFiles (pol, lay, KL)
IOPA public-coin interactive oracle proof with a fixed list of rounds, an instance, and external oracle strings that are fixed before the first message. The queried positions are functions of the instance and the challenges (in the prover's oracle messages also of the messages' plain parts). By its type, the decision takes the whole transcript; that it depends on the oracles at the queried positions alone is a separate property, InteractiveOracleProof.IsLocal.Iop.InteractiveOracleProof
configurationWhat the three IOPs share: index and instance types, two relations Ryes and Rno (no field relates them; in this protocol they are the same), the encoding of an index as a word of n symbols, seeds and answers, and the index decoder.Hiop.ConfigurationWithOutOfDomainSample; here DecR.configurationOfStoredTable A R
pads(1) Of the configuration: a value of the type Pad that hold places in the message beside the index. (2) Of a tenant: the entries reserved for its answers (see "seed; answer").ConfigurationWithOutOfDomainSample.Pad, hold; Msg.pad
committed tableThe encoded index as an external oracle string: 2^a symbols, which the verifier queries by position; a is the table depth. What is encoded is a message of field elements, indexed by row and entry.stored table; encoded index; oneExternalString (2 ^ a) SgX, ConfigurationWithOutOfDomainSample.E0
out-of-domain sample(1) Of a committed table: seeds, each a point and a nonzero factor, and the answers of every row to each seed. It is part of the instance of each of the three IOPs. In this protocol: one seed, a point of 29 coordinates and a nonzero factor, and one answer for each of the table's 2^v rows. (2) Of a tenant whose flag sampled is set: the verifier samples seeds in the round that sends it, and the prover's next message contains the answers.(1) record; ConfigurationWithOutOfDomainSample.Rec = Seed × Ans; RecFull (2) SymbolComponent.sampled
the offline IOPInstance: one out-of-domain sample. Oracle: one committed table. Three chains.Files.key; key file
the link IOPInstance: two out-of-domain samples. Oracles: two committed tables. One chain. In the Lean: the entry file.Files.entry; entry file; HolographicProtocol.link
the online IOPA request's proof. Instance: a request and one out-of-domain sample. Oracle: one committed table. Three chains.Files.proof; proof file
requestThe instance type of the online IOP. It is not printed in this appendix.XF := Flat.Req
full parameter sizeThe library has two fixed sets of size parameters. This protocol uses the larger one.frS, frP, recordLines against srS, srP, smallRecordLines
statement(1) A top-level statement: one of the theorems' statements on the argument system, in the main part of this document. (2) A chain's statement, in the byte format: a list of items; a committed table's root is held by one of them, whose number is the table's item. (3) The trivial statement: what an interactive oracle reduction reduces to when nothing is left to prove.(2) statement, itemRoot (3) Unit, extNone

How an IOP is written.

termwhat it means in this appendixthe Lean's word
written IOPAn IOP written in the format that this appendix prints: a value of FileDescription (three chains) or OneChainFileDescription (one chain).description
chainA consecutive part of an IOP that has a verifier state and a view of its own. The three chains are the fields first, shared, second, here called first, second, third (chains 1, 2, 3). Addresses and before number them 1 to 3; tree sources and BookPlan number them 0 to 2.Chain
segmentA part of a chain in which sub-protocols state claims and one sub-protocol, batch, is handed the function that gathers them.Link
sub-protocolThe unit in which an IOP is written: some rounds, their oracle messages and queries, and a step of the verifier's decision.Block
kindA family of sub-protocols: fifteen, each with a plain name; in Lean their labels are K1 to K15. (In Lean, Fmt.Kind is another thing, here called the challenge kind: what a round's challenge consists of, read off the round's name by Fmt.kindOf.)KindName, Kind; Fmt.Kind
addressThe location of a sub-protocol: chain, segment, number, kind. ("Position" is reserved for a queried position.)Place
verifier stateThe value that the verifier's decision carries from one sub-protocol of a chain to the next.S; "the carried record"
claimA value of the type Cl that a sub-protocol states from the verifier state, to be gathered for its segment's sub-protocol batch. What a claim asserts depends on the written IOP.Cl; Block.claims
schedule; declared roundA chain's schedule lists for each round a name and eleven numbers. A declared round is such an entry together with the committed tables that the round queries, each at its share of the sampled positions, and the Merkle trees that it opens.plan, Fmt.Entry; Fmt.DeclaredRound
matrix entriesValues in {−1, 0, 1} that a round's challenge may hold beside field elements and positions.Drawn.trits, Entry.trits; challenge kind entries
oracle message; tenantAn oracle message is the data under one Merkle root: 2^logLength symbols of a fixed number of words. Its tenants are the data that share its symbols, each with a fixed number of main and mask words in every symbol. A tenant's groups are numbers; the definitions printed here only compare these lists, and only add up the counts of main and mask words.Oracle; SymbolComponent
tree, root, to openThe schedule counts each oracle message as one Merkle root in its round's message; the message's tree is that commitment in the compiled protocol. A committed table has a tree too. "A round opens a tree" means: the verifier queries that oracle at the positions sampled in the round.Entry.roots, DeclaredRound.opens, Shape
shape; column; key; widthA shape is what a round declares of a tree that it opens: depth a, width W, whether it is a committed table's, the tree number. A column is the symbol at one queried position: a key, which names the oracle, the position, and W 64-bit words, each a base-field element.Fmt.Shape; OpenedColumn
round's values; viewA round's values are the items of the prover's message, Merkle roots left out, and the sampled challenge. A view is what the decision sees of one chain: its rounds' values and the list of opened columns.Fmt.RoundView; Fmt.View
public check; file checkA public check is a Boolean that depends on public data alone (the written IOP, the public files, what the planner returns), not on the instance or a view. The file check is the Boolean fileOk that a written IOP has as a field."test on the plan"; planOk; fileOk

From a written IOP to the protocol.

termwhat it means in this appendixthe Lean's word
round dataFor each chain the typed list of rounds from which the IOP's list of rounds is formed, with the table depth.OnBytes.Maker.WholeD; for the link IOP a list of RD
table queriesFor the link IOP: which round queries which of the two committed tables, at which share of the round's positions.XO (round, which, from_, count)
challenge-free roundA round in which the prover sends a plain message, no oracle, and the verifier's challenge has one possible value.plainRound
proof-of-work bitsFurther bits of a round's challenge, as many as the schedule entry's work. The verifier rejects unless all are 0.GChal, GChal.pass; Entry.work
round marking; NA marking says of each round of an IOP whether it is shared. N is the batch size: the number of batch positions. Neither is read by the definitions of the format or of the interpreter.RoundSplits; Files.N
hash oracleThe hash function, to which an algorithm has query access only.DeterministicAlgorithm, .query
second hash functionA second hash function of the byte format. The general description (theDescription) takes it as a parameter o; atSecondHashFunction substitutes the concrete function OnBytes.secondHashFunction for o. The six theorems are stated after this substitution.VerifierAndGoals.SecondHashFunctionType; OnBytes.secondHashFunction
a proof as submitted; typed proofA proof as submitted is a value of the type Form: for this protocol a list of tokens and five byte strings. The parser turns it into a typed proof: further tokens and two values in the compiler's types (KeyRoot, OfflineLinkOnlineProof).Form, FormBytes; TypedProof
compilerThe construction that turns the three IOPs, packed as Iop.HolographicProtocol, and further data into the non-interactive verifier. It is not printed in this appendix.innerCompiledVerifier, innerInputOfThreeProtocols
planner; planner's valuesThe functions that compute the schedules and sizes from the public files, the second hash function and a value in the digest's place. They are not printed in this appendix. The planner's values are what they return in the type FilesParameters.Key.madeAt, plannedAtO, ProofFile.Plain.planned; G
public parameters; makerPublic parameters are values computed from the public files, or written as constants, on which a written IOP or a sub-protocol depends: sizes, codes, numbers of rounds, declared rounds. A maker is a function that builds a written IOP, with its round data and its decision, from the public files or from public parameters.Key.Source, H2U.PlaceNums, Key.LaterPlaces; ProofFile.Pub; P14, P15, K1.Par, P2, P12. Makers: keyDataAndDecisionOrRefusalAt, proofDataAndDecisionOrRefusalAt, linkAt and what they call
partsA value of DescriptionData, DescriptionDataAtFiles or DescriptionFields: the components from which a Description is built."letters"

Words of the sub-protocols.

termwhat it means in this appendixthe Lean's word
groupA set of tenants, opened with one main code and one mask code, on which a proximity test is run. Linear constraints are imposed on a group until its test begins.Statement.groups; newGroupP, joinP, addRowsP; SymbolComponent.groups
tested, untested groupA group is tested once a proximity test has begun on it, untested before. A chain's last sub-protocol rejects if a group is untested, or a sampled tenant is in no tested group; the first two chains leave out one group, which the third chain tests.inRun; untestedL, untestedButOwnL
linear constraintA linear equation on the entries of tenants, with coefficients that the verifier computes and a target value. It is imposed on a group (after a fold: on the group's folded rows) and not checked there; the group's proximity test takes it as input. (A claim, by contrast, is gathered for its segment's sub-protocol batch.)OnBytes.Row, GroupRow
seed; answerA seed is a sampled point z with a sampled nonzero factor β. A tenant's answer y to a seed is sent by the prover and gives the linear constraint ⟨eq(z, ·), g⟩ + β·⟨θ, pad⟩ = y, where g is the tenant's entries outside the pads, the pad is a few entries reserved for that answer, and ⟨θ, pad⟩ weights them by the powers of a fixed element θ. A tenant's seeds and answers are its out-of-domain sample.rounds "SEND seed", "SEND answer"; cutSeeds, sampleRow
masked sumcheckA sumcheck on H + ε·S: the prover first sends the sum μ of a mask polynomial H, then ε is sampled, and the running claim starts at μ + ε·(the claimed sum). In each round the prover sends the round's polynomial without the one coefficient that the running claim fixes, and a challenge is sampled. No equation is checked round by round; one claim or one linear constraint is left.rounds "PSC …", "FOLD …"; pscBeginAt, pscRound; complete, after, hear
batchingOne element x is sampled; each of a list of claims or linear constraints is multiplied by a power of x fixed by its number, and all are added into one.rounds "BAT", "BAT-sigma"; weightNext, addOne; batch; chiOf
claim on the committed tableA linear equation ⟨g ⊗ eq(ψ, ·), M⟩ + (a form in mask entries) = target on the matrix M that the table encodes.TensorRow, WsClaim
stageOne level of a proximity test, given by a main code, a mask code and three numbers k, h, t. Every stage but the last has a fold of 1 + k rounds and a code switch of 2 rounds.Fmt.M1.Stage
code switchTwo rounds: the prover sends new oracle messages and seeds are sampled; the prover sends the answers and positions are sampled. Earlier oracle messages of the chain are opened at these positions, and the opened values give linear constraints on the new tenants, imposed on a new group.K2.codeSwitchKind; the proximity test's "the switch"; switchBehind
sealed chainA chain whose last round is the round named SEAL.chainEnd … sealed; sealRound
adoptedAn oracle message of an earlier chain is adopted by a later one: it is entered in the later chain's verifier state under its own tree number and source. Rejected unless it has a tree to itself, has the declared shape, and was sampled in the earlier chain under the same shape and codes.takeOver; adoptP, elsewhereP
arrayA numbered datum of the layout. An oracle-message sub-protocol inside a segment marks the arrays in its list as committed.arrays : Option (List Nat); commitOne
rows folded at a point; foldA table's or a group's rows folded at a point γ: the one row Σ_r eq(r, γ)·row_r. A fold, which occurs at the close of a segment and in a proximity test, is a masked sumcheck of 1 + k rounds whose challenges form such a point. It takes one linear constraint on a group and leaves one linear constraint on the group's rows folded there, its kept tenants and two mask rows.weights, eqTable; rounds "FOLD epsilon", "FOLD round"; foldD
base caseThe two rounds that end a proximity test. The prover sends a value τ*, and λ is sampled; the prover sends in the clear the message and tail of w* + λ·w and of u* + λ·u (w, u: the last tenant's main and mask word; w*, u*: a masking tenant's), and t positions are sampled. The oracle message that contains both tenants is opened there. Checked: ⟨c, M0⟩ + ⟨d, M1⟩ = τ* + λ·τ (M0, M1: the two messages sent; c, d, τ: the linear constraint that is left), and at each position x the re-encoded symbol equals w*(x) + λ·w(x), and likewise for u, at x's place in the shorter word.rounds "BASE lambda", "BASE"; baseDecide, baseChecks
product treeOver 2^D leaves, the binary tree of their products. A claimed value of a level at a point z is moved one level down by a masked sumcheck whose summand is the product of the two children's values vL·vR, followed by one sampled element ξ: the next point is (ξ, r), the next claimed value (1 − ξ)·vL + ξ·vR.level, stepDown, run; round "LINE"
shiftIn a lookup argument: a field element (theta in the Lean code) that is sampled before the point α where the parameters say so; the padding values and the table's rows are functions of it.Face.shifted; round "LKP shift"
keyUsed in "key file" and as the first component of a column, and nowhere else: a committed table's TableKey is "its out-of-domain seeds and answers"; Product-tree lookup argument's keys are "looked-up values".
  • The terms sub-protocol, segment, chain, claim, linear constraint, group, oracle message, tenant, seed, answer, masked sumcheck, batching, fold, code switch, base case and public check are used as defined in the appendix's table of terms.
  • Number and address: the sub-protocol's number in its chain, counted from 0, and its address ⟨chain, segment or –, number there⟩.
  • Kind: there are fifteen kinds, each listed here by its plain name, followed by its label in the Lean type KindName and a Lean definition of that kind (for the last two, the list that contains its sub-protocols).
  • "none" marks a sub-protocol without a kind: a row of the fold's own text, that is, a segment's frame or a chain's end (Lean: frame).
  • Oracle message with out-of-domain sample (K1; VerifiableInference.Desc.K1.sendOwn): two rounds. The prover sends oracle messages and out-of-domain seeds are sampled; then the prover sends the answers.
  • Code switch between segments (K2; VerifiableInference.Desc.First.K2.codeSwitchKind): two rounds. The prover sends oracle messages and out-of-domain seeds are sampled; then the prover sends the answers, and positions are sampled at which listed oracle messages of the same chain are opened.
  • Product-tree lookup argument (K3; VerifiableInference.Desc.K3.lookupKind): rounds that send no oracle message; it states the lists of claims objects, planes and guests in the offline IOP's form, and objects and guests in its other form (VerifiableInference.Desc.K3.Law.blockVia).
  • Layer-segment sumchecks (K4; OnBytes.Desc.First.K4.block): the rounds specific to a segment of layers, in which no oracle message is sent or opened; they leave the lists of claims front and back and a check after the batching.
  • Attention-segment sumchecks (K5; VerifiableInference.Desc.First.Att.P.attentionKind): the rounds specific to an attention segment, which send no oracle message; it takes its lists of claims as an argument.
  • Output-head sumchecks (K6; VerifiableInference.Desc.Kinds.Head.kind): the rounds specific to the output head, which send and open no oracle message and leave the lists of claims norm, policy and logits, with join inserted after the first (VerifiableInference.Desc.Kinds.Head.kindWithJoin).
  • Next-token message (K7; VerifiableInference.Desc.Kinds.Reply.kind): one round in which the prover sends the next token as one element and nothing is sampled; the verifier rejects if an element was already stored or the element is not a token of the vocabulary.
  • Draw of the approximate range proof (K8; VerifiableInference.Desc.First.K8.whole): the smallness test, consisting of one round that samples a matrix with entries −1, 0 or 1 and sends no oracle message, one list of claims, and two steps after the segment's batching.
  • Segment claim batching (K9; VerifiableInference.Desc.K9.batch): a segment's batching; two further sub-protocols of this kind come just before and just after the segment-closing row fold.
  • Segment-closing row fold (K10; VerifiableInference.Desc.First.Close.kind): 2 + k rounds that close a segment: a batching of linear constraints of the segment's group, then a fold of 1 + k rounds; no oracle message is sent or opened.
  • Output-head committed-table sumcheck (K11; Johnson.Desc.First.ForkMerge.headClaimMergeKind): lk + 4 rounds in the head's segment: a batching challenge and a masked sumcheck on the head's one claim on the committed table, which leave one claim; no oracle message is sent or opened.
  • Proximity test with linear constraints (K12; VerifiableInference.Desc.K12.proximityTestKind): a batching round; for each stage except the last, a fold of 1 + k rounds and a code switch of 2 rounds; then a base case of 2 rounds.
  • Committed-table claim merge (K13; VerifiableInference.Desc.K13.claimCombinationBlock): 2 + kCol rounds after the segments: one sampled element batches the two or more claims left on the committed table, and a masked sumcheck reduces them to one; no oracle message is sent or opened.
  • Committed-table claim reduction (K14; Desc.K14.blocks): the test on the committed table. Six sub-protocols in the second chain, around two sub-protocols of the kind "oracle message with out-of-domain sample", sample two points and the positions at which the table is opened, impose linear constraints and assign tenants to groups. One sub-protocol in the third chain (VerifiableInference.Desc.Third.batchLinearConstraintsSecondPart), with no rounds, adopts an oracle message of the second chain and adds a linear constraint.
  • Two-table comparison steps (K15; Desc.K15.linkBlocksBeforeTest): the link IOP's steps on its two committed tables, around a sub-protocol of the kind "oracle message with out-of-domain sample". They are: a sampled point; one sub-protocol with no round on the two tables' out-of-domain samples; sampled positions, with the first table opened at the first columnsFirst of them and the second table at the next columnsFurther; and a further sampled value, from which one linear constraint is added to the group.
  • Names of the chains in Lean: in the structure of a written IOP, the fields first, shared and second are the first, second and third chain, respectively. Names of the IOPs in Lean: the offline IOP is the field key of Files and the field offline of Iop.HolographicProtocol; the link IOP is entry and link; the online IOP is proof and, with its round marking, onlineBatch. Comments in the Lean code call the three IOPs the key file, the entry file and the proof file, after the files that contain their proofs.
  • Rounds, oracle messages sent: for one sub-protocol and for the full-size public files. Each oracle message is one Merkle tree and can have several tenants. A dash means that no value is given.
  • The offline IOP has 35 sub-protocols, the link IOP 8 and the online IOP 374: 417 in total. By kind:

inductive KindName where
| K1 | K2 | K3 | K4 | K5 | K6 | K7 | K8 | K9 | K10 | K11 | K12 | K13 | K14 | K15

| frame
deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

chain : Nat

piece : Nat
kind : KindName
deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

A schedule entry: a round's name and eleven numbers, including the numbers of proof-of-work bits, prover-message bytes, Merkle roots, sample answers, and sampled extension-field elements, positions and matrix entries.

structure Entry where
/-- the round's name -/
name : String
/-- how many rounds in a row are like this one (1 in every plan of a chain) -/
count : Nat := 1
/-- the bits of proof of work -/
work : Nat := 0
/-- the bytes of the prover's message that enter the query -/
msg : Nat := 0
/-- the roots among them -/
roots : Nat := 0
/-- the sample answers among them -/
answers : Nat := 0
/-- the elements of the extension field that are drawn -/
drawE : Nat := 0
/-- how many of these must not be 0 -/
drawNZ : Nat := 0
/-- the positions that are drawn -/
poss : Nat := 0
/-- positions are drawn below 2 ^ logN -/
logN : Nat := 0
/-- the matrix entries that are drawn -/
trits : Nat := 0
/-- for a round that batches rows: how many -/
rows : Nat := 0
deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

structure Shape where

a : Nat
/-- a column is a list of W elements of the base field -/
W : Nat

stored : Bool := false
/-- the tree's number -/
tree : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

structure Stored where
sh : Shape
/-- the bytes of a leaf's salt in this table's tree: the table's own number (R13.10), not
`Plan.salt`; it is no field of `Shape` -/
salt : Nat
/-- the number, from 0, of the statement's item that holds the root -/
item : Nat
/-- its part of the round's draws: from the draw number lo on, count of them -/
lo : Nat
count : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Inhabited

A committed table's share of a round's sampled positions: up to count positions starting at number lo (from 0).

def partOf (t : Stored) (poss : List Nat) : List Nat := (poss.drop t.lo).take t.count
DefinitionThe position number after the last share, if the tables' shares are contiguous starting at position number iFmt/Rules8X.lean:136–138
In words
In Lean · Fmt/Rules8X.lean, lines 136–138

If the tables' shares follow one another without a gap, starting at position number i, the result is the number of the position after the last share; otherwise it is none.

def partsFrom : Nat → List Stored → Option Nat
| i, [] => some i
| i, t :: ts => if t.lo == i then partsFrom (i + t.count) ts else none

True if a list of numbers is strictly increasing.

def increasing : List Nat → Bool
| a :: b :: l => a < b && increasing (b :: l)
| _ => true

Inserts a number into a strictly increasing list, unless it is already there.

def insertIntoIncreasingList (x : Nat) : List Nat → List Nat

| y :: l => if x < y then x :: y :: l else if x = y then y :: l else y :: insertIntoIncreasingList x l

structure Oracle where

logLength : Nat

words : Nat

DefinitionOne sub-protocol over state SJohnson/Desc/Block.lean:69–101
In words
In Lean · Johnson/Desc/Block.lean, lines 69–101

One sub-protocol, for verifier state type S and claim type Cl

structure Block (S Cl : Type) where
Labels

the name name, which labels its rejections

/-- for a refusal's words -/
name : String

the address place

place : Place
Public check

the public check planOk

/-- TESTS ON THE PLAN ALONE: no view, no record -/
planOk : Bool
Rounds

the declared rounds rounds, each with the committed tables and trees that it queries

/-- ROUNDS, and with them READS: for each round its entry of the plan (its name; what the message
holds; what is drawn), and the parts of stored tables and the trees that are opened at the
positions drawn in it -/
rounds : List Fmt.DeclaredRound

the oracle messages oracles: for each round, the oracle message under each root that the round sends

/-- ROUNDS: for each round, for each root that it sends: the oracle message beneath it -/
oracles : List (List Oracle)

the oracle messages before that must have been sent and, if sampled, have had their sample answered before the sub-protocol's first challenge. Each is given by its chain (1, 2 or 3) and its number, from 0, in that chain's order of sending

/-- FIXED BEFORE THE DRAW: the oracle messages that must have been sent, and where they are
sampled have had their sample answered, before this block's first draw: (the chain: 1, 2 or 3; the
message's number in its chain's order of sending, from 0). IT IS THE BLOCK THAT DRAWS A CHALLENGE
THAT NAMES THE MESSAGES WHICH ANY TEST HOLDS AGAINST THAT CHALLENGE, also a later block's test.
A BLOCK THAT SENDS A SAMPLED MESSAGE DOES NOT NAME IT HERE FOR THE DRAW OF ITS OWN SEEDS: the
answers come behind the seeds, so the test would refuse an honest plan; inside one block the order
"root, then seeds, then answers" is that of its own rounds -/
before : List (Nat × Nat)
Functions

the decision decide, which takes the verifier state, its rounds' values and the answers to its queries (one list of positions with their words for each table or tree opened) and returns the next state or a rejection

/-- DECIDES: from the record, its own rounds as a view shows them (no root; no sealed digest),
and just the columns that it is owed, grouped as the openings are (one group for each stored part,
then each tree, of each round), each column with its position: the next record, or a refusal
under the name of the test that refused -/
decide : S → List Fmt.RoundView → List (List (Nat × List UInt64)) → Except String S

the named functions claims: each takes the number of claims its segment has gathered so far and the state, and returns further claims with the state, or a rejection

/-- CLAIMS: named runs: each from the number of claims that the link has gathered so far and the
record, which holds what was heard, to claims and the record behind them, or a refusal. THERE IS
NO DEFAULT: a kind that has none writes []; one that forgets its run does not compile -/
claims : List (String × (Nat → S → Except String (List Cl × S)))

the named functions after: each takes the state after batching and returns the state or a rejection

/-- BEHIND THE BATCHING: named runs of a second sort: tests on, and writings into, the batched
form as it stands in the record behind the adding: the record handed on, or a refusal. No default
either -/
after : List (String × (S → Except String S))

The queries of a list of declared rounds, given each round's sampled challenge: for each round in turn, one list for each committed table that it queries and then one for each other Merkle tree that it opens. Each list consists of triples (key, position, width).

def groupsOf (firstTree : Nat) :
List Fmt.DeclaredRound → List Fmt.Drawn → List (List (Nat × Nat × Nat))
| d :: ds, R :: Rs =>
Tables

A committed table is queried at its share of the round's sampled positions, each taken modulo 2 ^ a, where a is the depth. Fmt.listOf sorts the positions in increasing order and removes duplicates. The key is Fmt.storedKey of the table's number, and the width is W of the table.

(d.stored.map fun s =>
(Fmt.listOf ((Fmt.partOf s R.poss).map (· % 2 ^ s.sh.a))).map fun x =>
(Fmt.storedKey s.item, x, s.sh.W)) ++
Trees

A tree is queried at all of the round's sampled positions, taken modulo 2 ^ a and ordered in the same way. The key is the tree's number minus firstTree, truncated at 0, and the width is W of the tree.

(d.opens.map fun o =>
(Fmt.listOf (R.poss.map (· % 2 ^ o.1.a))).map fun x => (o.1.tree - firstTree, x, o.1.W)) ++
groupsOf firstTree ds Rs
End

The result ends when either input list ends.

| _, _ => []

DefinitionRuns one sub-protocolJohnson/Desc/Block.lean:296–304

the file's variables

variable {Xi S Cl : Type}

Runs one sub-protocol: checks its rounds by roundsFit, checks that the next opened columns match its queries in key, position and width, then calls decide. Returns the next state and how many columns it consumed.

def Block.step (firstTree : Nat) (b : Block S Cl) (s : S) (rs : List Fmt.RoundView) (cols : List OpenedColumn) :
Except String (S × Nat) := do
need "the rounds" (roundsFit b.rounds rs)
let groups := groupsOf firstTree b.rounds (rs.map (·.drawn))
let want := groups.flatMap id
let got := cols.take want.length
need "the columns" (got.map (fun c => (c.1, c.2.1, c.2.2.length)) == want)
let s' ← b.decide s (rs.map noDigest) (regroup (groups.map (·.length)) got)
pure (s', want.length)

Looks up the claim function that o names (the index of a sub-protocol in bs, and a name) and runs it on the number of claims gathered so far and the state. It then runs the check each on o and on the claims and state that the function returned, appends those claims to the list and keeps that state. It rejects if there is no such function, or if the function or each rejects.

def claimsInStep (each : Nat × String → List Cl → S → Except String Unit) (bs : List (Block S Cl))
(x : List Cl × S) (o : Nat × String) : Except String (List Cl × S) :=
(named (o.2 ++ ": no such run") ((bs[o.1]?).bind fun b => b.claims.lookup o.2)).bind fun run =>
match run x.1.length x.2 with
| .ok y =>
match each o y.1 y.2 with
| .ok _ => .ok (x.1 ++ y.1, y.2)
| .error e => .error (o.2 ++ ": behind the run: " ++ e)
| .error e => .error (o.2 ++ ": " ++ e)

def chainAt (name : String) (firstTree : Nat) (bs : List (Block S Cl)) (s : S) (v : Fmt.View) :
Except String S :=

match foldBlocks firstTree bs s v.rounds v.opened with
| .ok (s', [], []) => .ok s'
| .ok (_, rs, cols) =>

def answeredIn : List Fmt.DeclaredRound → List Oracle → Nat → Bool
End

After the last round, due must be 0, and no remaining oracle message may have a tenant with an out-of-domain sample.

| [], os, due => due == 0 && saySampled os == 0
| d :: l, os, due =>
Each round

k is the number of tenants with an out-of-domain sample among the oracle messages that the round sends.

let k := saySampled (os.take d.entry.roots)

The round's answers must equal due.

d.entry.answers == due &&

If k ≥ 1, the round must be of kind seeds and have drawNZ ≠ 0, where drawNZ counts the sampled field elements that must be nonzero.

(k == 0 || (d.entry.drawNZ != 0 && Fmt.kindOf d.entry.name == some .seeds)) &&

In every case, due for the next round is k · drawNZ, which is 0 if k = 0.

answeredIn l (os.drop d.entry.roots) (k * d.entry.drawNZ)

variable {Xi S Cl : Type}

The verifier's decision for three chains, in order: public checks, instance check, field-range checks, chain 1 on its view with an empty round appended, chain 2, chain 3 started from both final states, final check.

def runCore {S₁ S₂ S₃ : Type} (planWord : Option String) (okStart : Bool) (s₁ : S₁) (s₂ : S₂)
(start₃ : S₁ → S₂ → Except String S₃) (firstTree₃ : Nat) (b₁ : List (Block S₁ Cl))
(b₂ : List (Block S₂ Cl)) (b₃ : List (Block S₃ Cl)) (fin : S₁ → S₂ → S₃ → Bool)
(v₁ v₂ v₃ : Fmt.View) : Except String (S₁ × S₂ × S₃) := do
if let some w := planWord then throw w
need "the test on the instance" okStart
need "a word of the first view is not below the prime" (viewWordsBelowPrime v₁)
need "a word of the second view is not below the prime" (viewWordsBelowPrime v₂)
need "a word of the third view is not below the prime" (viewWordsBelowPrime v₃)
let e₁ ← chainAt "the first chain" 0 b₁ s₁ (withEmptySealRound v₁)
let e₂ ← chainAt "the shared chain" 0 b₂ s₂ v₂
let s₃ ← match start₃ e₁ e₂ with
| .ok s => pure s
| .error e => throw ("the second chain's start: " ++ e)
let e₃ ← chainAt "the second chain" firstTree₃ b₃ s₃ v₃
need "the ends fail the last test" (fin e₁ e₂ e₃)
pure (e₁, e₂, e₃)

def descriptionFromSource (X : Source) (N : H2U.PlaceNums) (P : LaterPlaces) : FileDescription Xi :=
let Z := X.Y
let c := X.chains
let z := c.made.sized.key
let c₁ := firstChain Z.k.oneTime Z.D.1 Z.told.1 X.set N
let c₂ : Chain _root_.Desc.K14.St Claim := (sharedChain c P).retype
let c₃ : Chain VerifiableInference.Desc.Third.S₃ Claim := (thirdChain c P).retype
let len {σ : Type} (x : Chain σ Claim) : Nat := (x.blocksInOrder.flatMap (·.rounds)).length
{ S₁ := FirstState, S₂ := _root_.Desc.K14.St, S₃ := VerifiableInference.Desc.Third.S₃, Cl := Claim
plans := Z.D
wanted := wantedFirst Z.k.oneTime ++ wantedShared Z.k.shared.lin ++ wantedSecond Z.k.shared.lin
owed := owedFirst Z.k.oneTime ++ owedShared Z.k.oneTime Z.k.shared.lin ++ owedSecond Z.k.oneTime
tableDepth := Z.k.shared.lin.fold.index.tree.a
fileOk := (fileClauses X N P (len c₁) (len c₂) (len c₃)).all (·.2) &&
openedInBlocks
[VerifiableInference.Desc.oraclesOf c₁.blocksInOrder, VerifiableInference.Desc.oraclesOf c₂.blocksInOrder,
VerifiableInference.Desc.oraclesOf c₃.blocksInOrder]
(c₁.blocksInOrder.flatMap (·.rounds), c₂.blocksInOrder.flatMap (·.rounds), c₃.blocksInOrder.flatMap (·.rounds))
okStart := fun x => instanceOk X.Y.k.shared.lin x &&
_root_.Desc.K14.okKey (sharedPar c []) x.key
XiPub := Xi, pub := id
start₁ := fun _ => chainStart Z.k.oneTime.codes {}
start₂ := fun x => _root_.Desc.K14.first z.codes x.key
start₃ := fun _ s₁ s₂ => do
let f := firstOf s₁
let l ← named "the first chain's end names no W" s₁.lin
let e₂ ← named "the shared chain's end: something is untested" (_root_.Desc.K14.ended s₂)
VerifiableInference.Desc.Third.start₃E z.codes z.once.shape f.1 f.2.1 f.2.2.1 l.w l.own
l.mask f.2.2.2 (VerifiableInference.Desc.Third.sharedOfEnd e₂)
first := c₁
shared := c₂
second := c₃
fin := fun _ s₁ _ s₃ => firstEndOk Z.k.oneTime s₁ && VerifiableInference.Desc.Third.fin₃ s₃ }

The offline IOP's first chain: two sub-protocols that send oracle messages; a segment per lookup; the lookups' constraints imposed on one group; that group's proximity test; a batching of pending claims; optionally a third sub-protocol that sends oracle messages; the chain's last sub-protocol.

def firstChain (one : OneTime) (D : List Fmt.DeclaredRound) (told : List ProofFile.Root) (set : Setting)
(N : H2U.PlaceNums) : Chain FirstState Claim :=
let sent := rootsBefore D (batchRound D)
let first : Block FirstState Claim := sendIndexMasks one pieces (groupsTold told 0 (rootsAt D 0))
let front : List (Block FirstState Claim) :=
[sendOwnMessage one pieces (groupsTold told (rootsBefore D 2) (rootsAt D 2))]
let links := (lookupsOf one).zipIdx.map fun x => lookupLink one set x.2 x.1
let rng : Block FirstState Claim := rangesTest (enterRanges one) leaveRanges N
let back₀ : List (Block FirstState Claim) :=
[layRows one, rng, batchTableRows (·.keys) one pieces sent] ++
(sendW one pieces sent
(groupsTold told (rootsBefore D (lastSendRound D)) (rootsAt D (lastSendRound D)))).toList
let inFront : List (Block FirstState Claim) := first :: front ++ links.flatMap Link.blocksInOrder ++ back₀
{ first := first, front := front, links := links, back := back₀
last := firstChainEnd pieces (inFront.flatMap (·.rounds)) }

Takes the public parameters and the given sub-protocols. Returns an error message if baseOf returns one or, if anything is inconsistent or missing, an error message that lists it. Otherwise returns the result of onlineDescriptionAfterTests: the assembled written online IOP or a further error message.

def onlineDescriptionFromPublicPart (Z : Pub) (T : PureSeat) : Except String (FileDescription Inst) :=
(baseOf Z T).bind fun B =>
let faults := faultsAt T B
let P := partsAt T B
let lack := lackingAt T P
if !faults.isEmpty then
.error ("no description: the supplied blocks are inconsistent: " ++ "; ".intercalate faults)
else if !lack.isEmpty then
.error ("no description: nothing usable is supplied for: " ++ ", ".intercalate lack)
else onlineDescriptionAfterTests Z T P

def onlineDescriptionAfterTests (Z : Pub) (T : PureSeat) (P : PureParts) : Except String (FileDescription Inst) :=
-- `Except.bind` is written out: `FileDescription` lives one universe higher than what is bound here.
P.base.bind fun base =>
(chainBy Z base P.frames P.road).bind fun c =>
match T.shared, T.second with
| some A, some B =>
.ok (fileDescBy T.older T.links Z A B (fun s => s) (startS Z) c)
| _, _ => .error "no description: nothing usable is supplied for: a later chain"

Sub-protocols

the sub-protocol at each address, if there is one, block

block : Place → Option (Block S Cl)

the batching at each address, if there is one, batch

batch : Place → Option ((S → Except String (List Cl × S)) → Block S Cl)
Steps

the steps on the verifier state at the start of a segment, lay, and at its end, clear; each returns a new state or an error

/-- what is done to the state where a segment starts (`lay`) and where it ends (`clear`) -/
lay : Nat → S → Except String S
clear : Nat → S → Except String S
Checks

a segment's checks after each of its lists of claims, each

/-- a segment's test after each of its lists of claims: it is handed the segment's number, the
entry of the order, that list's own claims, and the state after the list -/
each : Nat → Nat × String → List Cl → S → Except String Unit

a segment's checks on the state after its batching, tests

/-- a segment's tests on the state after its batching, asked before what its blocks do after the
batching; they cannot change the state -/
tests : Nat → S → Except String Unit

a comparison of two states, same

/-- Guard (see `firstChain`): the two states have the same reply: `same before after`. That
it compares the reply, and the whole of it, is the matter of whoever supplies it -/
same : S → S → Bool
Ends

the chain's first sub-protocol, first

public data, in a block without a round; this file names no such test and asks none: a block that
asks nothing fits -/
first : Block S Cl

the chain's last sub-protocol, last

/-- the seal, the chain's last block: one round, the last entry of the plan -/
last : Block S Cl

Builds segment l of a given sort from the sub-protocols at the addresses determined by the lists of kinds, and fixes the order in which their claims are batched. Returns nothing if one of these sub-protocols is missing.

def linkAt (H : Blocks S Cl) (l : Nat) (sub : ModelPart) : Option (Link S Cl) := do
let ks := kindsBeforeBatching sub (l == 0)
let hear ← (addresses (some l) ks).mapM (blockAt H)
let a9 : Place := { chain := 1, link := some l, piece := ks.length + 1, kind := .K9 }
let batch ← H.batch a9
let close ← (closeAddresses l ks.length).mapM (blockAt H)
pure { name := s!"link {l}", chain := 1, number := l, lay := H.lay l, hear := hear,
order := orderOf sub, each := H.each l, orderAfter := orderAfterOf sub, tests := H.tests l,
batch := fun c => { batch c with place := a9 }, close := close, clear := H.clear l }

Builds the first chain from the list of the segments' sorts: the first sub-protocol, the segments, the sub-protocols after them, and the last sub-protocol. Returns nothing if the head is not the last segment, if it also occurs earlier in the list, or if a sub-protocol is missing.

def firstChainWithoutReplyGuard (H : Blocks S Cl) (links : List ModelPart) (several : Bool) : Option (Chain S Cl) := do
if !linksOk links then none
let ls ← links.zipIdx.mapM fun x => linkAt H x.2 x.1
let back ← (addresses none (backKinds several)).mapM (blockAt H)
let aS : Place := { chain := 1, link := none, piece := back.length + 1, kind := .frame }
let aF : Place := { chain := 1, link := none, piece := 0, kind := .frame }
pure { first := { H.first with place := aF }, front := [], links := ls, back := back,
last := { H.last with place := aS } }

(before : List (Nat × Nat)) (l : St → Clauses) (f : St → List Fmt.RoundView → Option St) :
Block St Unit :=
{ name := n, place := ⟨2, none, i, kind⟩, planOk := OkD.At.ofBlock n P.codes P.S
rounds := ((es.drop first).take k).map fun e => { entry := e }
oracles := oracles, before := before, decide := fun d rs _ => why (l d) (f d rs)
claims := [], after := [] }
let split1 := if P.S.sharedSplitNeeded then 1 else 0
let both := if P.S.sharedSplitNeeded then [(2, 1), (2, 2)] else [(2, 1)]
pure

number 1: the verifier samples a point

[{ plain "LIN point" 1 .K14 0 1 [[]] P.beforePoint (linPointL p) (linPoint p) with
planOk := OkD.At.ofBlock "LIN point" P.codes P.S && !P.beforePoint.isEmpty },

number 2: the prover sends an oracle message whose tenants are the table's rows folded at part of that point, and a mask

number 4: the verifier samples positions, at which the table is opened

rounds := ((es.drop 1).take 1).map fun e =>

oracles := [[]], before := [(2, 0)], decide := fun d rs gs => why [] (loc p d rs gs)

(behindOmega p),

number 6: the tenants of these messages are assigned to groups

number 7: the verifier samples a second point

number 8: it splits the linear constraint that equates the values of the two tenants at the two points into one constraint for each group, and has no round when there is only one group

{ name := "K1: a commitment", place := P.place, planOk := planOkOwn P && arrays.isSome

else .error "K1: the record does not stand at this place, or announces other messages" }

def lookupKind {S Cl : Type} (seat : SeatG S Cl) (before : List (Nat × Nat)) (bits : Nat)
(guests : List (First.Look.Guest S Cl)) (p : PG) : Block S Cl :=
{ name := p.name
place := ⟨p.chain, some p.link, p.piece, .K3⟩
planOk := p.planOk before bits guests
rounds := (p.entries.getD []).map fun e => { entry := e }
oracles := (p.entries.getD []).map fun _ => []
before := before
decide := fun s rs _ => do
let F ← named "K3: no ledger is open" (seat.fork s)
need "K3: rows are owed in front" (seat.owed s).noneWaits
need "K3: the ledger's count of slots" (F.next == p.first)
need "K3: the ledger's room" (F.ns == p.ns)
let x ← named "K3: the hearing" (hearG p F rs)
pure (seat.put s x.1 x.2)
claims :=
[("objects", fun _ s => do
let F ← named "K3 objects: no ledger is open" (seat.fork s)
let g ← named "K3 objects: nothing was heard" (seat.heard s)
pure (g.rows.toList.map seat.claim, seat.mark s (F.paid g.owedObjects))),
("planes", fun _ s => do
let F ← named "K3 planes: no ledger is open" (seat.fork s)
let g ← named "K3 planes: nothing was heard" (seat.heard s)
need "K3 planes: they are made once" (unpaidG F g.owedPlanes)
let x ← named "K3 planes: the leaves' claim" (planesG p.face g F [])
let l ← named "K3 planes: the caller's reader" (x.1.mapM (seat.claimP s))
pure (l, seat.mark s (x.2.1.paid g.owedPlanes))),
("guests", fun _ s =>
named "K3 guests: a guest refuses"
((guests.mapM fun (g : First.Look.Guest S Cl) => g.form s).map fun l => (l, s)))]
after := [] }

before := (p.matsIn ++ p.readsIn).map fun n => (1, n)
decide := fun s rs _ =>
match rs with
| [r] =>
if !seat.closed s then .error "the smallness test: the list of parts is open"
else if !seat.nothingOwed s then .error "the smallness test: a count of rows is owed"
else if seat.drawn s then .error "the smallness test: the matrix is drawn already"
else if seat.matrices s != p.ks.length then
.error "the smallness test: the record expects another number of matrices than \
the place's list has"
else if seat.ks s != p.ks then
.error "the smallness test: the record's matrices have other numbers of columns than \
the place's list"
else if seat.ms s != p.ms then
.error "the smallness test: the record's matrices have other numbers of rows than \
the place's list"
else if seat.tau s != p.tau then
.error "the smallness test: the record has another number of combinations than the place"
else if seat.tabs s != tabs p then
.error "the smallness test: the closed list of parts has other shapes than the place's"
else seat.lay s r.drawn.trits.toArray (firstColumns p)
| _ => .error "the smallness test: the block was handed another number of rounds than one"

after := [] }

variable {T Cl : Type}

Proximity test with linear constraints, taking its parts as an argument. Rounds: a batching round; for each stage except the last, a fold (1 + k rounds) and a code switch (2); a base case (2).

def proximityTestKind (X : Parts T) : Kind P12 T Cl := fun p =>
match p.nums.stages, H2U.roundsOfNums p.nums, H2U.testOracles p.nums with
| first :: rest, some rs, some os =>
let l : Laid := rs.zip p.oracles
let b : Block T Cl := ((((X.front p).at "the front" p.place []).andThen "the front"
((X.bat p ((l.take 1).map (·.1))).at "the batching" p.place (l.take 1))).andThen
"the batching"
(asks "the group is not the first stage's" p.place fun t =>
(X.group t).any (firstFits first))).andThen "the test"
(stagesFrom X p 0 first rest (l.drop 1))
{ b with
name := nameAt p.place, place := p.place, before := p.before
planOk := sizesOk p.nums.stages p.answers && rs.length == roundsIn p.nums.stages &&
p.oracles.length == rs.length &&
p.oracles.map (·.map fun o => (o.logLength, o.words)) == os && b.planOk }
| _, _, _ => { asks (nameAt p.place) p.place (fun _ => false) with planOk := false }
DefinitionThe parts of the proximity test with linear constraintsJohnson/Desc/K12/JoinGuarded.lean:225–258

In Lean · Johnson/Desc/K12/JoinGuarded.lean, lines 225–258

guardedProximityTestParts defines the parts that proximityTestKind takes as its argument, with further checks that cause rejection if they fail: (f) and (p) in the first part, (c), (k) and (g) in the batching, and (z) in every part that is given rounds. In the batching, one element is sampled. A fold is a masked sumcheck. In a code switch, the prover sends a new oracle message and earlier ones are opened at sampled positions. In the base case, the last message is sent in the clear in masked form and tested at sampled positions.

def guardedProximityTestParts : Parts T12 where
front := fun p =>
{ planOk := (frontJ p).planOk && H2K.FixedBefore.fixedOk p && H2K.First.cutOk p && p.early &&
p.answers == 1
decide := fun t rs gs => do
need "(f): the plan's count of roots in front of the test is not the record's"
(p.nums.free == t.roots)
let t' ← (frontJ p).decide t rs gs
need "(p): the record's codes or the place's rounds fail a public clause of the chain"
(H2K.Pub.pubOk p t'.st.codes)
pure t' }
bat := fun p cut => ranged cut
{ batJ p cut with
decide := fun t rs gs => do
need "(c): the group is not in order, or a batched row lies outside its members' tables"
(combOk t)
let t' ← (batJ p cut).decide t rs gs
need "(k): behind the batching the claim has a kept form, or the group a kept member"
(noKept t')
need "(g): the group's trees in the record are not those that the place's numbers declare"
(H2K.First.gpOk p t' && H2K.First.labelsOk p t')
pure t' }
fold := fun p j cur cut => ranged cut (foldJ p j cur cut)
switch := fun p j cur next last cut => ranged cut (switchJ p j cur next last cut)
batBehind := behindJ
base := fun p j cur cut => ranged cut (baseJ5 p j cur cut)
group := fun t =>
match t.pass, t.st.groups[t.g]? with
| .claim _ L, some G =>
match t.st.codes.base[G.code]?, t.st.codes.mask[G.maskCode]? with
| some c, some z => some (⟨c.logN, c.ell, c.r⟩, ⟨z.logN, z.ell, z.r⟩, L.k, L.h)
| _, _ => none
| _, _ => none
maskCame := fun t => t.mask.isSome

def claimCombinationBlock (X : Lens T) (p : Where) : Block T Cl :=
{ name := "K13: the batching"
place := ⟨p.chain, none, p.piece, .K13⟩
planOk := decide (1 < p.rows)
rounds := battRounds p
oracles := List.replicate (2 + p.lin.kCol) []

need "K13.batched-once" s.lin.isNone

pure (X.set t { s with owed := none, lin := some { claim := memberClaim o.1 }, d := o.2 })

after := [] }

batchLinearConstraintsSecondPart is the second part of the committed-table claim reduction and has no rounds. It first makes three checks and rejects if one fails (their names in Lean: "the two ends are at hand"; "the shape does not split the row (Dot)"; "no root is received yet, and the first own tree's number counts just one tree more"). It then adopts the oracle message named in the second chain's final state, adds it to the group named in this chain's state, and adds a linear constraint on that message and another tenant to the same group. Each of these steps can also reject. Its public check is the conjunction of lengthsOk, linOk and plainArm.

def batchLinearConstraintsSecondPart {Cl : Type} (p : P₁₄) : Block S₃ Cl :=
{ name := "K14, second part", place := ⟨3, none, 0, .K14⟩
planOk := p.codes.lengthsOk && linOk p.codes p.S && plainArm p.S
rounds := [], oracles := [], before := []
decide := fun s _ _ => do
let x ← named "the two ends are at hand" s.loc.border
need "the shape does not split the row (Dot)" (plainArm p.S)
need "no root is received yet, and the first own tree's number counts just one tree more"
(firstStepB s.roots s.loc.firstTree s.book)
let a ← takeOver p.S s.loc.own x.shared (s.withCols [])
let dot ← named "the row (Dot) can be made"
(linDotRow p.S x.g x.shared.psi a.1 (linLayOmega a.2.st.codes p.S) s.loc.w
(linLayW a.2.st.codes p.S))
let b ← named "the row (Dot) is laid" (addRowP a.2 s.loc.own dot)
pure { st := b.st, book := b.book, roots := b.roots
loc := { s.loc with border := none, omega := a.1 } }
claims := [], after := [] }

A chain's last sub-protocol. If the chain is sealed, it has one round, named SEAL, in which nothing is sent or read; otherwise it has none. Its public check is nothingOwedOnPlan on the rounds declared by the sub-protocols before it. It accepts if the given conditions on the verifier state hold.

def chainEnd {S Cl : Type} (chain piece : Nat) (sealed : Bool) (inFront : List Fmt.DeclaredRound)
(asks : S → Clauses) : Block S Cl :=
let rounds := if sealed then [sealRound] else []
{ name := "the end of chain " ++ toString chain, place := ⟨chain, none, piece, .frame⟩
planOk := nothingOwedOnPlan inFront, rounds := rounds, oracles := rounds.map fun _ => []
before := [], decide := fun s _ _ => (refuse (asks s)).map fun _ => s
claims := [], after := [] }
