DefinitionThe data that determine the argument systemLadder.lean:347–388
In words
In Lean · Ladder.lean, lines 347–388

The data that determine the argument system. These fields are functions of the public files: C (types, relation, encoding), the three IOPs F, the provers P, a hash-oracle algorithm readMore (also a function of the files' digest), the compiler data T (also a function of that digest and of the output of readMore), an extractor, the honest commit and prove, and the parser parse. The fields shown and the honest sample are not. There are also four types: More, Shown, Rand and Form.

structure Description where
/-- The types of indices and instances, the relation and the encoding. -/
C : PublicFiles → Hiop.ConfigurationWithOutOfDomainSample
/-- The protocols of the prover's three files: key file, entry file, proof file. -/
F : (Z : PublicFiles) → Files (C Z)
/-- Their honest provers. They stand in the types of keys and proofs (`F.withProvers P`); their values are
read neither by `innerCompiledVerifier` nor by any goal. -/
P : (Z : PublicFiles) → (F Z).Provers
/-- What the further public reading returns. -/
More : Type
/-- The further public reading: an algorithm with access to the hash function, from the public
files and their digest. -/
readMore : PublicFiles → Digest → DeterministicAlgorithm More
/-- The rest of what the compiler takes (see `InnerCompilerInputFieldsOverThreeProtocols`, Johnson/Flat/InnerInputOfThreeProtocols.lean), as a function
of the public files and of what the two public readings returned: among it how rounds and openings
are laid into queries, the coding of queries into the one hash function, the code of a key, and
how an instance is built from tokens. The goals let every field depend on the answers. -/
T : (Z : PublicFiles) → Digest → More → InnerCompilerInputFieldsOverThreeProtocols (F Z) (P Z)
/-- The extractor of `G8` and `G9` (and of `G8bits` and `G9bits`, Ladder/Bits.lean): one for all.
It sees the public files, the settings, the commitment and the committer's logged queries, and
nothing else: not the hash function, nor what the public readings returned. -/
extractor : PublicFiles → (s : IntegerTransformer.Settings) → Commitment → QueryLog →
Option (ModelWeights s)
/-- What a proof may reveal of the weights: its type. No goal here reads it. -/
Shown : Type
/-- What a proof may reveal of the weights. No goal here reads it. -/
shown : (s : IntegerTransformer.Settings) → ModelWeights s → Shown
/-- The honest committer's randomness: its type. -/
Rand : Type
/-- The honest committer samples its randomness. `G3'pol` reads it. -/
sample : RandomizedAlgorithm Rand
/-- The honest committer. `G3'pol` and `G9` read it. -/
commit : PublicFiles → (s : IntegerTransformer.Settings) → ModelWeights s → Rand →
DeterministicAlgorithm Commitment
/-- The form that the honest prover fills in. -/
Form : Type
/-- `D`'s own parser. `G3'pol` reads it. -/
parse : (Z : PublicFiles) → List Token → List Token → Form →
DeterministicAlgorithm (TypedProof (F Z) (P Z))
/-- The honest prover. `G3'pol` reads it. -/
prove : PublicFiles → (s : IntegerTransformer.Settings) → ModelWeights s → Rand → List Token →
List Token → RandomizedAlgorithm Form

Three public-coin IOPs over a configuration C. The offline IOP has an out-of-domain sample as its instance and the encoded index as its oracle. The link IOP has two of each. The online IOP has an element of type C.X together with a sample as its instance, and one encoded index as its oracle. The structure also contains N, the round markings, early and late.

structure Files (C : ConfigurationWithOutOfDomainSample) where
/-- the key file: on a record, over the encoded index -/
key : InteractiveOracleProof C.Rec C.E0
/-- the entry file: on two records, over two encoded indices -/
entry : InteractiveOracleProof (C.Rec × C.Rec) (twoExternalStrings C.n C.Sg)
/-- the proof file: on an instance and a record, over the encoded index -/
proof : InteractiveOracleProof (C.X × C.Rec) C.E0
/-- the number of slots -/
N : ℕ
/-- which rounds of the key file stand in its shared chain -/
annT : RoundSplits key.shape

reads := fun ρ =>
((wants₁ C D tF tJ t3 ρ ++ (wants₂ C D tF tJ t3 ρ ++ wants₃ C D tF tJ t3 ρ)).filterMap

let τ₁ := (chainsOf C D tF tJ t3).tr₁ τ

let w₃ := wantsOf D.a D.depth D.ds₃ R₃

Appendix B. The two hash functions

(1) blake2bHash is the function that leanVerifier uses in place of the random oracle. It is not plain BLAKE2b; it is computed as follows:

  • the bit string is first written as bytes;
  • the bytes are parsed as one call to the format's hash, Fmt.formatHash (a number, a tree, an index, a start, bytes), and the output is 32 bytes of BLAKE2b of that call, with bytes 0 to 15 of the start as salt and bytes 16 to 31 as personalization;
  • every other string, and a call with half 1 under a number other than 162, is hashed whole under one reserved number.

(2) secondHashFunction is the fixed function in the protocol's description: BLAKE2b's compression function with a number and the input's length in 32-bit words (rounded down) in the high word of the counter. In the statements, (1) is sampled at random and (2) is fixed.

let ⟨v0, v4, v8, v12⟩ := G s0 s1 v.v0 v.v4 v.v8 v.v12
let ⟨v1, v5, v9, v13⟩ := G s2 s3 v.v1 v.v5 v.v9 v.v13
let ⟨v2, v6, v10, v14⟩ := G s4 s5 v.v2 v.v6 v.v10 v.v14
let ⟨v3, v7, v11, v15⟩ := G s6 s7 v.v3 v.v7 v.v11 v.v15
let ⟨v0, v5, v10, v15⟩ := G s8 s9 v0 v5 v10 v15
let ⟨v1, v6, v11, v12⟩ := G s10 s11 v1 v6 v11 v12
let ⟨v2, v7, v8, v13⟩ := G s12 s13 v2 v7 v8 v13
let ⟨v3, v4, v9, v14⟩ := G s14 s15 v3 v4 v9 v14
⟨v0, v1, v2, v3, v4, v5, v6, v7, v8, v9, v10, v11, v12, v13, v14, v15⟩

def load64Plain (a : ByteArray) (k : Nat) : UInt64 :=
(byteOrZero a (k + 0) <<< 0) |||
(byteOrZero a (k + 1) <<< 8) |||
(byteOrZero a (k + 2) <<< 16) |||
(byteOrZero a (k + 3) <<< 24) |||
(byteOrZero a (k + 4) <<< 32) |||
(byteOrZero a (k + 5) <<< 40) |||
(byteOrZero a (k + 6) <<< 48) |||
(byteOrZero a (k + 7) <<< 56)

@[specialize] def updateBlocks (blk : Nat → MessageBlock) : (n i : Nat) → State → State
| 0, _, S => S
| n + 1, i, S => updateBlocks blk n (i + 1) (compress (incrementCounter S 128) (blk i))

@[inline] def finalBlock (S : State) (buf : MessageBlock) (buflen : Nat) : State :=
compress (setLastblock (incrementCounter S buflen.toUInt64)) buf

@[specialize] def message (blk : Nat → MessageBlock) (inlen : Nat) (S : State) : State :=
let n := (inlen - 1) / 128
finalBlock (updateBlocks blk n 0 S) (blk n) (inlen - 128 * n)

def blake2bSaltedPlain (salt personal data : ByteArray) (outlen : Nat) : ByteArray :=

Appendix C. The integer model

This appendix presents the integer model, from the definitions named in CanServe and requestOutcome (modelNextToken, RequestForm, requestResult) down to arithmetic.

The cards. A card names the definitions that it uses. Each of these, except those of Lean's own library, has its own card in this appendix (the five packed arrays of numbers are named but not printed). The small auxiliary definitions (such as entry, tabulate, sumOver, roundShift, clamp) are in the last folded section.

Range conditions. A range condition is a bound outside which the model is undefined (allConditionsHold).

The files. The Lean code is in IntegerModel/Model.lean (725 lines), VerifiableInference/ModelWeights.lean and VerifiableInference/RequestResult.lean, with one definition from IntegerModel/Window.lean; the first card is from VerifiableInference/Statements.lean.

The comments in the Lean code. A short comment at the end of a Lean line, such as -- Vx or -- sigma, gives the symbol for that value in docs/model.md ("The integer model"); "section 7" in two comments refers to a section of that file. The numbers 1 to 8 in the comments of the range conditions enumerate these conditions. The definitions can be read without these comments.

The model's result on a request · 6 cards
DefinitionThe model's tokens on a request, or failureVerifiableInference/RequestResult.lean:68–74
In words
In Lean · VerifiableInference/RequestResult.lean, lines 68–74
Given

settings, weights at these settings (ModelWeights),

def requestResult (settings : Settings) (weights : ModelWeights settings)

a prompt and a claimed output

(prompt output : List Nat) : Option (List Nat) :=
Run

the model is run on one window of 1,024 tokens: the prompt, the claimed output, then zeros (zeroFilledWindow)

let window := IntegerModel.zeroFilledWindow prompt output
Value

if the model has a value on this window (modelNextToken returns some token):

if (modelNextToken settings weights window).isSome then

the choices of this run (trace, its field choices, one for each of the 1,024 positions)

let choices := (trace settings lookupTables weights.val window.toArray).choices.toList

the result is some list of these choices, starting at position prompt.length - 1 (0 for an empty prompt): as many as the claimed output has tokens, or fewer if the window ends first

some ((choices.drop (prompt.length - 1)).take output.length)

if the model has no value on this window (modelNextToken returns none), the result is none: failure

else none
Remark
  • The two lists are arbitrary: RequestForm is not tested here.
  • The range conditions are tested at all 1,024 positions, including the positions padded with zeros, so a failure can be caused by a position after the output.
  • The run reads the claimed output, so the result is a function of both lists.
DefinitionThe form of a requestVerifiableInference/RequestResult.lean:46–48
In words
In Lean · VerifiableInference/RequestResult.lean, lines 46–48
Given

settings, a prompt and an output

def RequestForm (settings : Settings) (prompt output : List Nat) : Prop :=
Holds if
  • every token of the prompt and of the output is below settings.vocabulary
  • neither list is empty
(∀ token ∈ prompt ++ output, token < settings.vocabulary) ∧ output ≠ [] ∧ prompt ≠ [] ∧
  • the two lists together have at most 1,025 tokens
prompt.length + output.length ≤ 1025
Remark
  • It depends only on the vocabulary size and the two lists, not on the weights or on settings.positions (the number 1,025 is a literal).
  • 1,025 is one more than the number of positions in the window (zeroFilledWindow), so the window does not contain the 1,025th token.

Given

an exponent bits, a shift, an offset eps; a vector x of integers

def rmsNorm (bits shift : Nat) (eps : Int) (x : IntegerVector) : Norm :=
Run

the sum of the squares of x's entries

let sumSquares := sumOver x.size fun k => x.entry k * x.entry k

the integer square root (integerSquareRoot) of that sum plus eps (of 0 if that is negative)

let root : Int := integerSquareRoot (sumSquares + eps).toNat

2 to the power bits, plus half of root, divided by root

let reciprocal := (2 ^ bits + root / 2) / root

each entry of x times reciprocal, divided by 2 to the power shift and rounded (roundShift)

let quotient := x.map fun xk => roundShift (xk * reciprocal) shift

each of these clamped to the interval from −2,047 to 2,047 (clamp, activationBound)

let out := quotient.map fun wk => clamp wk activationBound
Value

all five, in one structure (Norm)

{ sumSquares, root, reciprocal, quotient, out }

Value

the values below, in one structure (Attention)

Attention :=
Run

the normalization of each row (rmsNorm), with the layer's exponent, shift and offset

let norm := x.map fun row => rmsNorm p.attentionBits p.attentionShift p.attentionEps row -- step 1

at each position t: queries, keys and values from the normalized row (projections)

let projected := tabulate x.size fun t => projections s p tables w t (norm.entry t).out -- steps 2, 3

at each position, for each query head: its attention (attendHead)

let heads := tabulate x.size fun i => tabulate s.queryHeads fun h => attendHead s p tables projected i h -- step 4

at each position: the heads' results concatenated, s.queryWidth entries

let mixed := tabulate x.size fun i => tabulate s.queryWidth fun j =>
((heads.entry i).entry (j / s.headDim)).out.entry (j % s.headDim)

each such row times the output matrix, each entry divided by 2 to the power p.outputShift and rounded

let addition := mixed.map fun o => (product o w.output s.width).map fun e => roundShift e p.outputShift -- step 5

at each position: the row of x plus that row (addVectors)

let out := tabulate x.size fun t => addVectors (x.entry t) (addition.entry t)

the layer's weights w; a position t; a vector a (in attention: the normalized row at t)

(w : LayerWeights) (t : Nat) (a : IntegerVector) :
Value

the values below, in one structure (Projections)

Projections :=
Run

the cosines: if p.rotary, row t of the cosine table; else s.headDim / 2 entries, each 2 to the power s.rotaryScale

let cosine :=
if p.rotary then tables.cosine.entry t else tabulate (s.headDim / 2) fun _ => 2 ^ s.rotaryScale

the sines: if p.rotary, row t of the sine table; else as many zeros

let sine := if p.rotary then tables.sine.entry t else tabulate (s.headDim / 2) fun _ => 0

a times the query matrix (product): s.queryWidth entries

let queryProducts := product a w.query s.queryWidth

a times the key matrix: s.keyValueWidth entries

let keyProducts := product a w.key s.keyValueWidth

both rotated by these cosines and sines, pair by pair within each head (rotate)

let rotatedQuery := rotate cosine sine s.headDim queryProducts
let rotatedKey := rotate cosine sine s.headDim keyProducts

each entry divided by 2 to the power p.queryShift (for keys: p.keyShift) and rounded (roundShift)

let wideQuery := rotatedQuery.map fun e => roundShift e p.queryShift
let wideKey := rotatedKey.map fun e => roundShift e p.keyShift

each entry clamped to the interval from −2,047 to 2,047 (clamp): the queries and the keys

let query := wideQuery.map fun e => clamp e activationBound
let key := wideKey.map fun e => clamp e activationBound

a times the value matrix, each entry divided by 2 to the power p.valueShift and rounded

let wideValue := (product a w.value s.keyValueWidth).map fun e => roundShift e p.valueShift

each entry clamped in the same way: the values

let value := wideValue.map fun e => clamp e activationBound

DefinitionThe rotary position embeddingIntegerModel/Model.lean:319–323
In words
In Lean · IntegerModel/Model.lean, lines 319–323

rotate applies the rotary position embedding: in each head of headDim entries of A (headDim even) it maps the entries (a, b) at 2i and 2i + 1 to (c * a - s * b, s * a + c * b), with c = cosine[i] and s = sine[i].

def rotate (cosine sine : IntegerVector) (headDim : Nat) (A : IntegerVector) : IntegerVector :=
tabulate A.size fun j =>
let i := (j % headDim) / 2
if j % 2 = 0 then cosine.entry i * A.entry j - sine.entry i * A.entry (j + 1) -- p0 = C A0 - S A1
else sine.entry i * A.entry (j - 1) + cosine.entry i * A.entry j -- p1 = S A0 + C A1

distances : IntegerVector -- u_ij

the exponentials

In Lean · IntegerModel/Model.lean, lines 382–398
Given

the settings s; the layer's settings p; the lookup tables

def attendHead (s : Settings) (p : LayerSettings) (tables : Tables)

the queries, keys and values of all positions; a position i; a query head h

(projected : Array Projections) (i h : Nat) :
Value

the values below, in one structure (Head)

Head :=
Run

dh: the number of entries of one head

let dh := s.headDim

g: h divided by the number of query heads for each key and value head

let g := h / (s.queryHeads / s.keyValueHeads) -- the key and value head that query head h reads

for each position j from 0 to i: the inner product of head h's query at i and head g's key at j

let scores := tabulate (i + 1) fun j =>
sumOver dh fun c =>
(projected.entry i).query.entry (h * dh + c) * (projected.entry j).key.entry (g * dh + c)

the largest of these scores (maxUpTo)

let top := maxUpTo (fun j => scores.entry j) i

for each score: top minus the score, divided by 2 to the power p.softmaxShift

let distances := scores.map fun sj => (top - sj) / 2 ^ p.softmaxShift

for each distance, its exponential: the entry of the exponential table at that distance, or 0 if the distance is not less than the table's size

let exponentials := distances.map fun (u : Int) =>
if u < tables.exponential.size then tables.exponential.entry u.toNat else 0

the sum of these exponentials

let total := sumOver (i + 1) fun j => exponentials.entry j

for each entry c of a head: the sum over j of j's exponential times entry c of head g's value at j

let mix := tabulate dh fun c =>
sumOver (i + 1) fun j => exponentials.entry j * (projected.entry j).value.entry (g * dh + c)

each of these sums, doubled, plus total, divided by twice total

let out := mix.map fun acc => (2 * acc + total) / (2 * total)
Value

all seven

{ scores, top, distances, exponentials, total, mix, out }

def wellFormed (s : Settings) (tables : Tables) (weights : Weights) : Bool :=
Holds if

the numbers of key-value heads and query heads are positive, and the first divides the second

0 < s.keyValueHeads && 0 < s.queryHeads && s.queryHeads % s.keyValueHeads == 0

the width of a head is positive and even; the vocabulary is not empty

&& 0 < s.headDim && s.headDim % 2 == 0 && 0 < s.vocabulary

there are no experts, or s.hidden is twice s.expertHidden

&& (s.experts == 0 || s.hidden == 2 * s.expertHidden)

the final normalization's offset and its shift are at least 1

&& 1 ≤ s.finalEps && 1 ≤ s.finalShift

the lookup tables for cosine and sine have s.positions rows, each of half a head's width

&& hasSize s.positions (s.headDim / 2) tables.cosine &&
hasSize s.positions (s.headDim / 2) tables.sine

the table for the exponential is not empty, its first entry is positive, and no entry is negative

&& 0 < tables.exponential.size && 0 < tables.exponential.entry 0 &&
(tables.exponential.all fun e => 0 ≤ e)

the table for SiLU has all keys from −32,768 to 32,767, and the table for the sigmoid has all keys from −16,384 to 16,383

&& tables.silu.covers (-32768) 32767 && tables.sigmoid.covers (-16384) 16383

the embedding matrix has s.vocabulary rows of s.width entries, and the matrix weights.head has s.width rows of s.vocabulary entries

&& hasSize s.vocabulary s.width weights.embedding && hasSize s.width s.vocabulary weights.head

there are settings and weights for exactly s.layers layers

&& s.perLayer.size == s.layers && weights.perLayer.size == s.layers

in each layer, the matrices that the layer reads have the sizes given by the settings, and the two offsets and the shifts passed to roundShift are at least 1 (layerWellFormed; softmaxShift is not tested)

&& (List.range s.layers).all fun l =>
layerWellFormed s (s.perLayer.entry l) (weights.perLayer.entry l) (s.isMixture l)

lookupTables is the Tables value made of the five tables on the next cards, with lowest key -32,768 for SiLU and -16,384 for the sigmoid.

def lookupTables : Tables where
cosine := cosineTable
sine := sineTable
exponential := exponentialTable
silu := { lowestKey := -32768, entries := siluTable }
sigmoid := { lowestKey := -16384, entries := sigmoidTable }

cosineTable has 1,024 rows, one for each position, each with 64 entries, one for each pair of entries of a head. Entry pair of row position is entry 64 * position + pair of the packed array Inst.Model.Data.cos (packedEntry, 14 bits), minus 4,096, clamped to the interval from -4,096 to 4,096.

def cosineTable : Matrix :=
tabulate 1024 fun position => tabulate 64 fun pair =>
clamp ((packedEntry Inst.Model.Data.cos 14 (64 * position + pair) : Int) - 4096) 4096

siluTable has 65,536 entries; entry index corresponds to the key index - 32768. The key is first clamped to -16,384 .. 16,383. The entry is then the entry of the packed array Inst.Model.Data.silu at the clamped key plus 16,384 (packedEntry, 13 bits), minus 4,095, clamped to -4,095 .. 4,095. Below and above these keys the table is constant.

def siluTable : IntegerVector :=
tabulate 65536 fun index =>
clamp ((packedEntry Inst.Model.Data.silu 13
(min (max ((index : Int) - 32768) (-16384)) 16383 + 16384).toNat : Int) - 4095) 4095
